findings.F1: Step 5's result is on the side the idea predicts but short of the bar: a mean unusual move of +0.70 % over 5 days, t 1.79 on 990 cases. My own recount of the cases, the first positive-forecast bar in each 5-day cell, gives +0.79 % with t 2.05 on 1009 cases. The verdict therefore sits right at the threshold, and how the cases are counted is enough to move it across.
findings.F2: The mean comes from a few large rises, not from the typical break. The median unusual move over 5 days is -0.95 % and only 44.9 % of cases rise more than the drift. Skew is 1.59 and excess kurtosis 10.1. Trimming 5 % from each tail cuts the mean to +0.24 %, and winsorising at 1 %/99 % gives t 1.94.
findings.F3: The effect is uneven across coins. ZEC carries most of it, at +4.1 % over 5 days (t 2.65, 141 cases). BTC gives +1.1 % (t 1.84) and ETH +0.7 % (t 0.90). LTC is flat at +0.2 %, and XMR (-0.6 %) and XRP (-0.2 %) are below their drift.
findings.F4: The effect is drowned in bear years even with the 60-day-return and 50-day-average gate in place. In 2018 the 5-day unusual move is -6.6 % (t -2.58, 36 cases) and in 2022 it is -3.2 % (t -2.78, 74 cases). In 2019 it is +2.7 % (t 2.52, 114 cases) and in 2024 +2.6 % (t 2.34, 133 cases).
findings.F5: The grading the idea claims does not show in the cases. Larger distance above the 50-day average does not bring a larger rise: Spearman is -0.02 over 5 days and -0.06 over 20 days. The top fifth of distance gives +1.1 % against +1.5 % for the second fifth. The touch count times margin is also flat: Spearman -0.05, with quintile means between +0.5 % and +1.3 %.
findings.F6: A longer horizon makes the move larger but not clearer. Strength grows from 0.067 at 5 days to 0.12 at 20 days and 0.14 at 30 days. But the t on each horizon's own non-overlapping grid stays about 2: 2.05 at 5 days (1009 cases), 2.00 at 10 days (675), 2.01 at 20 days (411) and 1.87 at 30 days (304). Changing the horizon gives no clearer answer than adding cases.
findings.F7: The size easily covers the cost of a trade. The total move of +1.27 % per case is 6.6 times the 0.19 % round trip, and the unusual move alone is 3.6 times it. The book passed every profitability check (Sharpe 1.00 against holding's 0.55). Size is not the problem; the problem is too few independent cases for a fat-tailed move, and the 13 coins outside the default data are available on daily bars.

ideas.name: resistance breakout uptrend, all coins
ideas.idea: When a coin closes above a price where it turned down several times in the past 90 days, it tends to keep rising over the next 5 days, only while its 60-day return is positive and its close is above its 50-day average, and the further its close stands above that average, the larger the rise.
ideas.consequence: A break of a repeatedly held level is a reason to buy only when the coin already trades well above its 50-day average; a break made from below or near that average, as in the bear phases that carry the book's deepest falls, is a reason to stay out.
